house_rules: Every proof routes through the operator's declared canary collector (scope.csv class canary, http_probe with canary=True) - a DNS log or HTTP hit on a third-party service is gossip, not channel proof (organ doctrine).
Payloads below are canonical forms from the public record, attributed per entry.
Egress toward cloud metadata endpoints is an authorized-only action: the scope row must cover the HOST the request actually lands on, not just the URL the parameter names.
failure_modes are mandatory reading BEFORE closing a hypothesis as negative: a bypass that failed for a listed reason leaves the filter untested, not effective.

prerequisites: sink fetches attacker-named URLs with a permissive scheme handler
entries.oracle: file contents in the response body or a body-hash differential vs a nonexistent path
failure_modes: scheme allowlist (http/https only) - the refusal itself is a FACT about the sink's validation posture
response body never surfaced - pair with a canary-readable transform (error text, size oracle) instead of assuming failure

prerequisites: gopher handler reachable in the sink's URL stack
internal TCP service (Redis/MySQL/SMTP) in egress reach
entries.oracle: the internal service state changes / answers - Redis MONITOR or the service's observable side effect is the proof; bounded to a self-owned proof key
failure_modes: gopher stripped by URL validation - try gophers:// or the secondary handlers (dict://, ftp://) before closing
egress firewall drops the port regardless of scheme
the proof must be reversible (DEL the proof key) - never leave state on client infrastructure

source.title: A New Era of SSRF (gopher/protocol abuse)

entries.technique: alternate IP notations against string filters
entries.oracle: request lands on the loopback/private address the filter tried to block - canary callback or response differential proves resolution
failure_modes: sink normalizes the URL before validation (modern parsers resolve then check) - the class is dead at THAT sink; verify with the exact sink version, libraries differ
DNS-layer resolution of the odd form fails on some stacks - each variant is a separate FACT record, not one class

source.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - SSRF (bypassing filters)

entries.technique: redirect-based pivot (validator checks first hop only)
prerequisites: attacker-controlled URL that can 302 to an internal target
entries.oracle: internal response body/hash surfaces via the followed hop; the redirect host must be operator-owned (scope row canary or in_scope)
failure_modes: validator re-checks EVERY hop - per-hop validation kills the pivot
redirect protocol restrictions (https->http downgrades refused)
metadata endpoints answer non-200 to default UA - read the class-specific entry (SSRF-006..008) for the required headers

source.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - SSRF (bypassing filters via redirects)

prerequisites: sink resolves the hostname TWICE (once to validate, once to fetch)
entries.probe: http://{{rebind-domain}}/ - first resolution answers a public IP, second answers 127.0.0.1
entries.oracle: the fetch lands on the internal address after the validation pass; proof via canary callback from the internal hop
failure_modes: sink pins the resolved IP after validation (resolve-once) - the gap is closed at that sink
DNS caching between the two resolutions - TTL games need the cache window measured, not assumed
operator needs a rebinding-capable DNS setup - scope.csv canary row for the DNS host, never an unlisted third-party rebinder

source.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - SSRF (DNS rebinding class)

prerequisites: SSRF egress to 169.254.169.254 from an AWS workload
entries.oracle: role list, then per-role credential document - names/key prefixes visible in the response; NEVER copy full credentials into the ledger (mask at first 8 chars, artifact under engagements/, report states the class)
failure_modes: IMDSv2 enforced: GET returns 401 - token flow (PUT with X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds) must be reachable THROUGH the SSRF (PUT-capable sinks only); if not, the class is closed and the hardening is a positive FACT
hop-limit 1 blocks container/pod egress paths
response template strips keys - use the size/hash oracle instead

source.title: AWS EC2 User Guide - Instance metadata and user data

prerequisites: egress to metadata.google.internal (or 169.254.169.254) from a GCP workload
sink can send the required header
entries.oracle: 200 + project metadata tree; the header requirement is itself the detection differential (bare GET = 403/redirect)
failure_modes: sink cannot set arbitrary headers on the fetched request - header injection via the URL is a separate hypothesis, not assumed
workload identity hardened scopes - tokens listed but cloud-platform scope absent limits impact; record as scope FACT

prerequisites: egress to 169.254.169.254 from an Azure workload
entries.oracle: JSON instance document (compute/network/identity blocks) in the response
failure_modes: api-version parameter mandatory - a bare GET is refused, which is itself the Azure fingerprint
managed identity absent - identity block empty; impact bounded to information disclosure

prerequisites: two components parse the SAME URL differently (validator vs fetcher) - the parser-chain map first
entries.oracle: validator reads one host, fetcher reads the other - request lands on the host the validator missed; canary callback from the fetch proves which parser won
failure_modes: single parser does validate+fetch (no seam) - URL confusion needs TWO disagreeing components, same law as desync-hunter's seams
WHATWG-compliant parsers on both sides - confusion surface shrank to backslash/encoded-slash cases; test the exact library pair, ledger versions

entries.technique: operator canary channel proof (the house entry)
prerequisites: scope.csv row class canary for the operator collector (with artifact)
entries.probe: payload URL host pointing at the declared collector: https://{{collector}}/collect/{{marker}} - the SSRF itself places the URL in the sink parameter
entries.oracle: a GET poll on the collector (canary mode: GET-only, no query string, bounded path) returns the marker - the CHANNEL is proven end-to-end: server-side request -> collector -> operator poll, every hop ledgered CANARY
failure_modes: the canary gate refuses the URL (query string or path slack) - that refusal is doctrine working, re-shape the payload within the channel rules
no callback after differential says the fetch happened - egress filtering between sink and collector; try the redirect entry (SSRF-004) as the delivery path
a third-party interaction host responding instead of the operator collector = gossip, never a CONFIRMED channel record
